response.content:
For the cyclohexanone, the only α-carbon that can form an enolate is the less hindered C-6 side, giving Michael addition adjacent to the carbonyl; this matches ethyl 3-(3-ethyl-1,3-dimethyl-2-oxocyclohexyl)propanoate.

For 1-nitropropane adding to (E)-but-2-enenitrile, the nitronate carbon adds to the β-carbon of the unsaturated nitrile, giving NC–CH2–CH(CH3)–CH(NO2)–CH2–CH3, i.e. 3-methyl-4-nitrohexanenitrile.

Answer: A
